segments.label: Clinical trials
segments.why: Eligibility criteria, cost, and risk assumptions often default to male bodies or exclude women of childbearing age.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Dosage, side effects, and effectiveness become less reliable for women.
segments.real_world: A medication that seems “safe” can produce unexpected side effects or weaker efficacy in underrepresented groups.
segments.what_to_fix: Recruitment targets, sex-disaggregated reporting, and trial designs that treat hormonal variation as normal—not noise.

segments.label: Pain scales
segments.why: Women’s pain is more likely to be downplayed or reframed as stress/anxiety.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Symptoms get dismissed, delayed, or misclassified.
segments.real_world: Longer diagnostic journeys and lower trust in care systems.
segments.what_to_fix: Structured symptom capture, clinician training, and protocols that treat subjective pain reports as valid data.

segments.label: Emergency symptoms
segments.why: Textbook symptom profiles often reflect male patterns as ‘typical’.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Non-typical presentations are missed or triaged lower.
segments.real_world: Higher risk of delayed care for conditions like heart events.
segments.what_to_fix: Update guidelines, train for variation, and build triage tools using diverse symptom profiles.

segments.label: AI diagnosis
segments.why: Models learn what’s in the data. If women are underrepresented or labeled differently, bias becomes ‘accuracy’.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Confident predictions that are wrong for certain groups.
segments.real_world: Automation can scale inequity quietly and fast.
segments.what_to_fix: Bias audits, balanced datasets, subgroup evaluation, and transparent model reporting.

segments.label: Drug dosage
segments.why: Metabolism differences and hormonal cycles are under-accounted for in standards.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Over- or under-dosing and unpredictable side effects.
segments.what_to_fix: Sex-specific dosing studies and stronger monitoring/post-market reporting.

segments.label: Endometriosis
segments.why: Normalization of pain + slow research investment leads to long delays.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Symptoms are reframed as ‘normal periods’ or stress.
segments.real_world: Years to diagnosis, reduced quality of life, and mental health burden.
segments.what_to_fix: Faster referral pathways, research funding, and better symptom screening tools.

segments.label: Mental health
segments.why: When symptoms are unclear, clinicians may default to psychological explanations—especially for women.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Physical conditions become invisible behind mental health labels.
segments.real_world: Patients stop seeking care or feel unheard.
segments.what_to_fix: Dual-track assessment: investigate physical causes alongside mental wellbeing, not instead of it.

segments.label: Wearable data
segments.why: Sensors and models often assume ‘default’ physiology and activity patterns.
segments.what_goes_wrong: Tracking becomes noisier or misleading for some bodies.
segments.what_to_fix: Inclusive calibration, validation studies, and user controls for context (cycle, pregnancy, etc.).
